subject: Data tiering & scrub policy: decision log for MedCore PHI retention
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Huang <emma.huang@medcore.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data tiering & scrub policy: draft proposal + questions

Emma / team —

Attaching a concise draft of a proposed data tiering and scrub playbook for PHI/PII ingested via the MedCore integration (attached: redwood-data-tiering-proposal-20260814.pdf). Key points for the decision:

- Proposed retention windows by tier:
  - Hot session/cache: 30 days (fast KV cache, ephemeral)
  - Short-term working set: 90 days (searchable)
  - Long-term archive: up to 7 years (encrypted, immutable snapshot)

- Redaction vs deletion options under consideration:
  - Field-level irreversible obfuscation (cryptographic hash with salt + truncation) — retains analytic counts but removes direct identifiers
  - Reversible tokenization (customer-managed KMS) — supports re-identification for legal requests but increases attack surface and audit burden
  - Full irrevocable deletion (secure wipe) after archival retention

Questions where we need MedCore input to finalize:
1) Legal hold / eDiscovery expectations — duration and what triggers a hold?
2) Residency constraints: do you require EU-only storage for any of these records? (We can pin archive buckets to region.)
3) Any fields you require preserved in reversible form for downstream workflows (e.g., patient IDs used by your billing backend)?

Technical notes included in the draft: how prefix- and KV-caching will be excluded from long-term archives, and a recommended schedule for rolling scrubs and audit proofs.

Action requested: please reply with preferences on (1) reversible tokenization vs irreversible hashing for identifiers and (2) residency constraints. We'll then produce a final decision playbook and a prioritized implementation ticket.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0183

Attachment: redwood-data-tiering-proposal-20260814.pdf (2 pages)

From: Emma Huang <emma.huang@medcore.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Hold (MedCore) <legal@medcore.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data tiering & scrub policy: draft proposal + questions

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear summary and the draft. A few immediate notes from MedCore side:

- Legal hold: typically 2–3 years after a triggering incident for a retained record, but eDiscovery can extend this; we need an ability to freeze deletion per-case.
- Residency: EU residency required for any EU patient records; US records can stay in US. We will provide a list of country scopes per data feed.
- Re-identification: our billing and outcomes team need deterministic mapping for patient IDs for a rolling 18–24 month reconciliation window. After that window, irreversible hashing is preferred.

Can you confirm how legal-hold overrides would be implemented operationally (stop-delete flag, separate hold index, etc.)? We also need to ensure archived exports for audits can be produced within 10 business days.

Cc'ing Legal for any additional constraints.

—Emma
Emma Huang
Head of Procurement, MedCore Health
emma.huang@medcore.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data tiering & scrub policy: draft proposal + questions

Laura / Ben —

Technical comments after reviewing the draft and Emma's reply (see inline):

- Legal-hold implementation: we can implement "hold" as a metadata flag on the tenant object and on individual record IDs. Deletion jobs will consult the hold index; records with an active flag are queued into an eDiscovery retention bucket and excluded from purge. Export tooling can surface those buckets for Legal.

- Reversible tokenization vs hashing:
  - Deterministic hashing (HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific salt) gives deterministic mapping without storing keys, but is irreversible. That meets analytics and reconciliation only if MedCore is willing to use hashed IDs in their backend.
  - Reversible tokenization requires storing the token map encrypted under a customer KMS key; it supports re-identify flows but requires stricter access controls and auditing.

- Performance / cost tradeoffs:
  - Short-term searchable data increases storage and index cost (we should advise MedCore on a cost delta estimate).
  - Archive encryption and region pinning add egress/replication considerations for EU residency (we can pin to eu-west-1 and use a dedicated archiving bucket).

I've attached an ops matrix that maps choices to impact on cost, SLA, and compliance (ops-scrub-options-matrix-20260815.csv). Suggest we keep deterministic reversible tokens for the 18–24 month reconciliation window if MedCore insists, then schedule a migration to irreversible hashing post-window.

-Markus

Attachment: ops-scrub-options-matrix-20260815.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Huang <emma.huang@medcore.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data tiering & scrub policy: draft proposal + questions

Thanks all — summary and proposed decisions (finalize unless objections by EOD Wednesday):

1) Residency: honor region-by-patient rule. EU patients' records will be stored/archived in EU-only buckets. (Action: Monica to capture the country mapping feed from MedCore.)

2) Reconciliation window and tokenization:
   - Keep reversible tokenization for identifiers needed by MedCore workflows for 18 months. Token maps encrypted with customer KMS; access limited to a small SRE+Legal role.
   - After 18 months, run irreversible transform (HMAC with tenant salt) and purge token maps. This satisfies your analytics and reduces long-term risk.

3) Legal hold: implement as a per-record metadata flag that excludes records from purge. Exports for legal review served from a dedicated retention bucket; we will guarantee 10 business days for export delivery.

4) Retention windows: hot 30d / working 90d / archive 7y default. We will expose tenant-configurable overrides if MedCore requires different floors.

5) Audit and proof of deletion: implement tamper-evident deletion logs (hash chain) and provide monthly audit reports for the first year.

Next steps and owners:
- Monica Patel: get country-to-feed mapping from MedCore by Tue 2026-08-18.
- Ben Carter: draft SLA language for export timelines + legal-hold behavior by Fri 2026-08-21.
- Markus Klein: schedule token-map lifecycle job and scrub job in INF-4392.
- Laura: prepare final playbook and send to MedCore with the implementation timeline.

If no objections, I'll upload the finalized playbook and route to Legal for sign-off.

Thanks,
Laura
